harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Created a LUKS2-encrypted file-backed volume on node1 mounted at /srv/secure, configured to auto-unlock (via a root-only keyfile referenced in /etc/crypttab) and auto-mount (via /etc/fstab) at boot with no manual intervention. Verified across a full node reboot: boot_id changed, systemd-cryptsetup@secure.service and the fstab mount both came up active automatically, and the test file written before reboot was readable afterward.
actions_performed: Installed cryptsetup on node1
Generated a 4096-byte random keyfile at /etc/luks-keys/secure.key (mode 400, root:root)
Created a 2GiB sparse backing file /var/lib/luks-volumes/secure.img and formatted it as LUKS2 using the keyfile
Opened the LUKS container as /dev/mapper/secure and formatted it XFS
Added /etc/crypttab entry (secure, backing file, keyfile, luks,nofail) so systemd-cryptsetup-generator auto-unlocks it at boot
Added /etc/fstab entry (UUID=..., /srv/secure, xfs, defaults,nofail) so it auto-mounts at boot
Verified manual mount, wrote a test file, then unmounted/closed and re-triggered via systemd-cryptsetup@secure.service to simulate boot path
Captured pre-restart baseline (boot_id, mount state, cryptsetup status, test file contents)
Rebooted node1 via systemd-run scheduled reboot, returning the ack before disconnection
Polled node1 until exec was available again and confirmed boot_id changed
Verified post-restart recovery: /srv/secure mounted, cryptsetup status active, test file readable, relevant systemd units active

evidence.requirement: Encrypted volume exists and is mounted at /srv/secure, backed by cryptsetup/LUKS
evidence.summary: cryptsetup installed; LUKS2 container created on a file, opened as /dev/mapper/secure, formatted XFS, and mounted at /srv/secure with test file written and read back

evidence.requirement: Volume unlocks and mounts automatically at boot (no manual intervention)
evidence.summary: crypttab/fstab entries added; after manual close, triggering systemd-cryptsetup@secure.service (the same unit systemd runs at boot) auto-unlocked the volume and it mounted per fstab, with test file intact
Captured boot_id d052eb57-c81d-4309-ae7f-bce362073ff9, active mount, active LUKS mapping, and readable test file before reboot

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart acknowledgement returned before disconnect
evidence.summary: systemd-run scheduled a delayed reboot and the ack ('reboot scheduled') returned successfully before the node disconnected

evidence.requirement: Proof node1 actually restarted (changed boot identity)
evidence.summary: Connection dropped during reboot, node was unreachable for several poll attempts, then came back with boot_id f8b3e503-df03-4a7d-8286-5087c4cdd521 (different from baseline) and uptime since 08:10:09

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of encrypted volume, data, and service state
evidence.summary: After reboot, /srv/secure is mounted from /dev/mapper/secure, cryptsetup status shows active LUKS2 mapping, test file content 'hello-encrypted' still present, and systemd-cryptsetup@secure.service is active — all without manual intervention
